summary.text: Alma Adams is the Democratic incumbent for North Carolina's 12th Congressional District. A former Bennett College art professor, she served on the Greensboro school board and city council and in the North Carolina House before winning a November 2014 special election to Congress. She serves on the House Agriculture and Education and Workforce Committees; her official biography highlights work on HBCU funding and Black maternal health.

paragraphs.text: Alma Adams was born in High Point, North Carolina, and attended high school in Newark, New Jersey, according to WFAE's 2026 voter guide.

According to her official biography, she graduated from North Carolina A&T State University in 1968, received a master's degree in art education in 1972, and earned a Ph.D. in art education and multicultural education from The Ohio State University in 1981.
She taught art at Bennett College for 40 years, according to her official biography, and led student voter-participation efforts there.

Adams began her political career in the 1980s as the first African American woman elected to the Greensboro school board, then served nine years on the Greensboro City Council before moving to the state legislature.

She was appointed to North Carolina House District 26 in 1994 and served ten terms, including as chair of the North Carolina Legislative Black Caucus; her official biography credits her with the Displaced Homemakers Bill and the state's first minimum wage increase in nine years.

Adams won the November 2014 special election for the 12th District and was sworn in immediately as the 100th woman elected to the 113th Congress; she was elected to her sixth full term on November 5, 2024.

She serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology; Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress, and previously served on the Committee on Financial Services (2019-2022).

Her official biography lists the enactment of H.R. 5363, the FUTURE Act (permanent funding for Minority-Serving Institutions), among her legislative accomplishments; she founded and co-chairs the Congressional Bipartisan HBCU Caucus and co-founded and co-chairs the Black Maternal Health Caucus, which introduced the Momnibus package.
She has received the North Carolina A&T State University Human Rights Medal and was inducted into the National Black College Alumni Hall of Fame, according to her official biography.
